subject.title: Slack: Include file attachment metadata in inbound message delivery to agents

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared inbound attachment metadata contract for agent context, or keep Slack attachments represented only by placeholders plus MediaPath/MediaTypes for now?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable fix changes a shared channel/plugin context contract and may affect third-party plugin expectations, so automation should not choose the permanent API shape alone.

options.title: Add Shared Attachment Metadata
options.body: Introduce a cross-channel metadata field carrying provider ids, names, MIME types, sizes, local/download references, and downloaded status while preserving legacy media fields.

options.title: Keep Current Placeholder Contract
options.body: Document that Slack file IDs are intentionally exposed through placeholders and download-file, and defer structured metadata until a broader context redesign is prioritized.

options.title: Prototype Slack-Only Metadata
options.body: Add a narrow Slack field first, accepting the risk that it may need migration if sibling channels adopt a different shared shape later.

recommendation.title: Add Shared Attachment Metadata
recommendation.body: Introduce a cross-channel metadata field carrying provider ids, names, MIME types, sizes, local/download references, and downloaded status while preserving legacy media fields.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent adjacent Slack media work make vincentkoc the best available owner for the shared media/context API decision.
